**A product treats one zero as decisive.** In multinomial Naive Bayes, a document's class score multiplies probabilities for its words. If a word never appeared in the spam class, a naive frequency estimate assigns it probability zero, making the entire document likelihood zero for spam regardless of all other words. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

Additive smoothing gives every vocabulary term some probability mass. If a class contains 100 word occurrences, vocabulary size is 20, and alpha=1, an unseen word gets probability $1/(100+20)=1/120$. A word seen nine times gets $(9+1)/120$. The denominator increases too, so the probabilities still sum to one.

**Log space fixes a different problem.** Multiplying hundreds of small positive probabilities can underflow to numerical zero. Adding their logarithms preserves useful relative scores. But log(0) is negative infinity, so switching to logs alone does not solve the unseen-word problem. You need both smoothing and stable arithmetic.

Build the vocabulary from training data and specify treatment of truly out-of-vocabulary terms. Conditional independence is a simplifying assumption: related words can count overlapping evidence repeatedly, making probabilities overconfident. Naive Bayes can still rank or classify effectively, but probability calibration should be assessed separately.

**Technical details and references.**

A zero estimated class-conditional word probability makes the whole multinomial likelihood zero if that word occurs. Additive smoothing reserves positive probability for unseen vocabulary terms. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

$$P(w\mid c)=\frac{count(w,c)+\alpha}{\sum_vcount(v,c)+\alpha V},\quad score(c)=\log P(c)+\sum_wcount(w,d)\log P(w\mid c).$$

Log space prevents numerical underflow from multiplying many small probabilities; it does not fix zeros by itself, since $\log0=-\infty$. Smoothing and log arithmetic solve different problems. Define the vocabulary from training data and specify handling of out-of-vocabulary terms. Conditional independence is an approximation; correlated words can make Naive Bayes probabilities overconfident even when classification is useful.
